content:
maria: quick check — local tests suddenly getting 401s when using the SDK. env var looks fine in terminal but SDK sends Authorization header with trailing space? anyone seen weird trimming differences across runtimes?
joel: which SDK/lang?
maria: node, @joel. running in docker. I noticed when I cat'ed /run/secrets/API_KEY it has a newline. export API_KEY=$(cat /run/secrets/API_KEY) — maybe includes newline.
caro: yep, newline can break base64/basic header if you do `echo $API_KEY | base64` vs `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | base64`. `echo` may add a newline.
maria: here's what I tried:
```
# bad (adds newline)
export API_KEY=$(cat /run/secrets/API_KEY)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# safer (strip CR/LF explicitly)
export API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n' < /run/secrets/API_KEY)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
joel: Node specifics: Buffer.from(key).toString('base64') is fine, but double-check you aren't wrapping the key in extra quotes during a CI step (e.g., JSON.stringify) — that will change the header. Also `echo "$KEY" >> file` in GH Actions will append a newline unless you use `echo -n`.
maria: another gotcha — I was building Basic header from an old snippet (username:password) while the current integration expects `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`. switched to Bearer and 401s went away.
ben: FYI: Redwood SDKs accept API keys in the `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header by default. Basic is only for HTTP basic auth (username:password). If you must use Basic for a proxy, make sure the base64 is exactly `base64(username:password)` with no trailing newline.
caro: TL;DR: trim CR/LF from secret files, prefer `tr -d '\r\n'` or `printf '%s'`, avoid `echo` in pipelines, and confirm Bearer vs Basic. :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks all — patching Dockerfile and GH Actions. will ping when the staging run passes.
